discovery.none: No automatic LAN discovery protocol is documented for this replacement firmware; use the DHCP assignment shown by the router or enter the rabbit address manually.

identification.notes: A provisioned rabbit has no documented mDNS/SSDP identity. Find its DHCP address at the router or select it manually. The setup AP name is Nabaztag<XX>; do not identify arbitrary stock rabbits as running this replacement firmware without checking their configuration.

device.name: Nabaztag/tag (ServerlessNabaztag replacement firmware)
device.notes:
SCOPE: this spec is for a Nabaztag/tag after installation of ServerlessNabaztag replacement firmware. It is not the stock rabbit's v1 polling or v2 XMPP protocol, and it does not cover Karotz.
The rabbit serves HTTP on its own address at the root paths in http_endpoints. The separate configured platform host supplies firmware and resources below /vl; that host is not the rabbit and /vl is not a prefix for the rabbit's local action routes. Basic actions are device-local once the replacement firmware and resources are installed. Weather, NTP, AI, and arbitrary resource fetching have separate external dependencies declared in protocol_details.external_dependencies.

openness.notes: Open replacement firmware with a published device-local OpenAPI. No stock Violet/Mindscape server protocol is claimed, and no licence is inferred for the repository because the reviewed root has no licence file.

upstream_docs.covers: Every device-local route, method, parameter, encoding, and declared response.

enter_pairing_mode.notes: There is no pairing-mode exchange in the OpenAPI. The setup AP is a provisioning state, not proof of client pairing.

pairing.notes: OpenAPI 1.1.0 declares no security scheme, but the README also mentions optional simple password protection without defining its HTTP behavior. Consequently the need for credentials on a configured rabbit is unknown, not an assertion that every route is open. Implement the documented unauthenticated requests only where the owner's configuration permits and do not guess an auth mechanism.

unpair.notes: Revocation for an optional web/Telnet password is not documented.

credentials.notes: The setup page uses plain HTTP. The README mentions optional simple password protection for web and Telnet but does not specify its API exchange, so no Authorization header, cookie, pairing token, or default credential is invented. The OpenAI API key and TTS signing secret belong only on the AI relay, never on the rabbit.
stored_on_device: Optional owner-configured web/Telnet login settings, if enabled

factory_reset.description: Use the setup sequence to change configuration, not as evidence of a complete erase. Firmware replacement and factory reset are separate.
factory_reset.effect: Not established. The head-button sequence enters setup mode; the README does not establish that it erases Wi-Fi credentials, settings, scripts, or paired clients, and no separate factory-reset procedure is asserted.

methods.description: Hold the head button while applying power, release when every LED is blue, then use the configuration page at 192.168.0.1. Set the Violet Platform to andreax79.github.io/ServerlessNabaztag without an HTTP scheme, or to a self-hosted plain-HTTP server holding the vl folder. The firmware appends /vl itself.
methods.name: Head-button setup AP and platform host

credential_encryption.notes: The configuration page is plain HTTP. Any Wi-Fi passphrase or settings entered there have no TLS protection. The README does not specify the form fields or an application-layer cipher.

steps.action: Unplug the rabbit, hold the button on its head, and restore power while continuing to hold it.
steps.expect: All lights turn blue; release the head button.

steps.action: Join the Nabaztag<XX> setup Wi-Fi network and open http://192.168.0.1.
In General Info, set Violet Platform to andreax79.github.io/ServerlessNabaztag or a trusted self-hosted equivalent, without http://. Do not add /vl manually.
steps.expect: The platform host has no scheme and the firmware can derive its /vl resource root.

steps.action: Select Update settings and wait for the rabbit to reboot.
steps.expect: The rabbit joins its configured network and serves the root HTTP UI/API on its DHCP address.

steps.action: Find the assigned address at the router and open the root web interface; configure optional services only after choosing their external dependencies.
steps.expect: Device-local routes such as /status respond on the rabbit, not on the /vl platform host.

setup.notes: Setup installs the replacement firmware, joins the setup AP, and points the rabbit at a plain-HTTP platform host. The published flow has not been replayed here. Self-hosting the vl directory removes the dependency on the project's GitHub Pages resource host but not the need for a resource host during installation and resource updates.

rejoin.notes: Re-enter the same head-button setup AP to change network/platform settings. No factory reset is required by the published setup flow.

steps.action: Hold the head button while applying power and release when all lights are blue.
Open http://192.168.0.1, update the desired settings, select Update settings, and wait for reboot.
steps.expect: The rabbit returns with the new configuration.

testing.notes: Transcribed from ServerlessNabaztag 63e654955aadffeff82786d03d345cd6e910d230, vl/api/openapi.yaml version 1.1.0 and README. No rabbit, SoftAP, local HTTP route, resource host, NTP service, weather service, or AI relay was contacted. Host tests exercise the document, not physical hardware.

artifacts.description: Replacement firmware, device-local OpenAPI, setup flow, resource platform, and AI relay documentation.

evidence.documentation_review: Read the replacement project's README and OpenAPI 1.1.0 at commit 63e654955aadffeff82786d03d345cd6e910d230. Every one of the 34 operations is represented with its original method, parameter schema, body encoding, and response. External dependencies and relay-secret boundaries come from README, not invented route security schemes.
evidence.open_questions: OpenAPI does not define response-object fields, error responses, security schemes, or numeric code labels. The README's optional password protection and NTP defaults are not expanded into guesses.

covers: Device-local action, ear, LED, sound, sleep/wake, status, settings, and advanced routes
Direct LED status setting without a weather/stock/traffic provider
not_covered: Stock Nabaztag v1/v2 or Karotz protocols
NTP and weather freshness without their configured providers
AI without the relay and its external service
Arbitrary MP3/resource fetching without a reachable plain-HTTP source
The unspecified optional web/Telnet authentication flow
local_access.summary: ServerlessNabaztag puts an HTTP API on the rabbit itself after replacement firmware and a resource platform are configured. Direct root actions do not require the old Violet/Mindscape cloud. External resources and optional services retain the separate dependencies listed above.

action_semantics.service4_service5: Integer with no OpenAPI range or labels; do not invent one.

ai.default_state: Assistant and experimental wake word disabled by default.
ai.direction: Rabbit -> plain-HTTP LAN relay -> TLS/WSS OpenAI service
ai.impact: AI turns and experimental wake word are unavailable without the relay/external service; non-AI local actions are independent.
ai.provider: Owner-configured stateful Node.js realtime relay and its external OpenAI connection
ai.relay_requirements: Node.js and FFmpeg on a trusted LAN host; restrict the relay port to that LAN.
ai.secret_rule: OPENAI_API_KEY and TTS_SIGNING_SECRET exist only in the relay's protected environment. They are never accepted by /setup-ai, stored in rabbit flash, exposed through /status, or sent over the rabbit's plain-HTTP hop.

ntp.impact: Automatic time and time-dependent sounds/schedules can be wrong or stop when unavailable.
ntp.local_alternative: Configure a trusted LAN NTP server.
ntp.provider: Configured NTP server; hostname and port are not specified by the reviewed OpenAPI/README

resource_fetch.local_alternative: Serve the MP3 from a trusted LAN HTTP server.
resource_fetch.requirement: Plain HTTP only; HTTPS is unsupported. Availability and content are outside the rabbit-local API.

weather.impact: Weather and air-quality refresh stop when the provider is unreachable; direct LED and other basic local actions remain separate.
weather.local_alternative: A compatible trusted-LAN provider or manually set /weather and /pollution codes.
weather.provider: open-meteo, per README; exact endpoints are outside OpenAPI

lifecycle.firmware_update: Resource installation is an owner-led replacement-firmware operation. No generic firmware-upload endpoint or safe update procedure is declared here.
lifecycle.stop_scope: /stop halts current movements and sound; /abort plays a sound. Neither is represented as a universal emergency stop for external tools or AI-invoked actions.
lifecycle.telnet: README also describes a Forth Telnet service on port 22 and configurable login settings; its authentication and protocol are outside the OpenAPI and this spec.

documentation_routes.openapi_json: http://{nabaztag_ip}/openapi.json (README documentation, not an operation declared in the OpenAPI paths object)

openapi.encoding: Percent-encode query values and application/x-www-form-urlencoded fields once. In particular, a leading # in an LED color is %23 on the wire. Do not send JSON for the three form operations.

200.description: A JSON object with the device's status.

query_parameters.description: Plain HTTP relay host:port without scheme.
query_parameters.name: u

query_parameters.description: Tool manifest URL; empty derives /ai_tools.json from the configured server.
query_parameters.name: o

200.description: A JSON object with the tasks status.

openapi.response_rule: Only the declared statuses are asserted: 204 with no documented body for commands, or 200 application/json for /status, /animations, /tasks, and /forth. JSON object properties are intentionally unspecified.
openapi.route_case: Case-sensitive; preserve every path and single-letter parameter exactly.
openapi.server: http://{nabaztag_ip}; root paths on the rabbit itself

platform_host.derived_root: The firmware appends /vl to the configured host.
platform_host.direction: Rabbit -> configured HTTP platform server for firmware and resources; separate from client -> rabbit root API.
platform_host.self_host: Copy the repository's vl directory into a plain-HTTP server directory named vl and configure that server without http://.
platform_host.warning: Never rewrite a rabbit-local /status, /left, or other action to the platform host, and never prefix those rabbit-local routes with /vl.

remaining_unknowns: Exact optional web/Telnet authentication mechanism and whether a given configuration requires it on root API routes.
Property schemas for /status, /animations, /tasks, and /forth responses; OpenAPI declares only JSON objects.
Human meanings of numeric nose/weather/stock/traffic/mail codes beyond the published ranges.
Factory-reset existence and erase scope; head-button setup mode is not evidence of erasure.
NTP provider defaults, speech-service backing for /say, and exact external weather/resource endpoints.
All operations are source-reported and untested against a rabbit by this project.
